raw_response:
I have farmed this land a long time, so I will not do anything fancy. I will start from what worked before and look at what the men around me are doing. Fertilizer costs real money, but if I cut too hard and the yield falls, that loss hurts more, so I will keep the rates a little on the safe side. My family has some off-farm work, so I also need work that I can finish on time. On my 14 mu, I will keep most land in the wheat-maize rotation because that is the steady way here, and I will leave a smaller piece for cotton. I will put 10 mu into wheat-maize and 4 mu into cotton. For wheat, I will use the same kind of improved seed most neighbors use now, put enough base fertilizer under it, and water it twice with the well if the season is normal. After wheat harvest, I will put hybrid maize back on that same 10 mu, mostly with no-tillage to save labor and catch the moisture, then give it two waters if the rain is not enough. Cotton takes more watching, more spraying, and more hand work, so I will keep only 4 mu of it. I will feed it a bit heavier with potash than wheat and maize, because if cotton is short of strength later, the bolls do not hold well. I will not chase very high yield with expensive input, but I will not go light either.
